title: Generate Governed Shared Parameter TXT from Registry
purpose: Generate and release a shared-parameter TXT carrier directly from the governed central Shared Parameter Registry so the registry remains the authoritative source and released TXT files remain derived implementation artifacts.

applies_to.scope: Generation, validation, release, and archival of governed shared-parameter TXT carriers

preconditions: The governed central Shared Parameter Registry is available and readable.
Release scope is defined; by default only Citizen and Active rows are included unless a Candidate has explicit approval.
The selected generation path can preserve exact GUID, name, group, and type values.
A governed distribution location exists for released TXT files.

steps.name: Confirm registry version and release scope
actions: Identify the registry version and release date context.
Filter to Citizen and Active rows unless an explicitly approved exception applies.
Stop if in-scope collisions or unresolved identities remain.
validation: The release scope is traceable to a specific registry state.
No unresolved in-scope identity is silently included.
failure_modes: Unresolved collisions remain in release scope.

steps.name: Extract governed export set
actions: Extract GUID, Name, Group, and Type for every in-scope registry row.
Retain additional descriptive fields only as validation metadata where needed.
Check GUID uniqueness and duplicate GUID/name pairs.
validation: The export set contains one governed definition per included GUID.
No duplicate GUID or duplicate GUID/name pair exists.

steps.name: Generate TXT from governed registry values
actions: Start from an empty base or governed template rather than an arbitrary project TXT.
Create every included parameter with the exact governed GUID, Name, Group, and Type values.
Save to a temporary working release file before publication.
validation: Generated definitions preserve the registry values without alteration.
failure_modes: Generation changes an identity or structural field.
An arbitrary project TXT is reused as the authoritative source.

steps.name: Validate TXT against registry
actions: Compare every in-scope registry GUID against the generated TXT.
Confirm identical name, group, and type values.
Confirm the TXT contains no extra parameters outside the release set.
Regenerate after correcting the registry or generation process if discrepancies exist.
validation: There are no missing, altered, or extra parameter definitions relative to the governed release set.
failure_modes: TXT differs from the governed registry extract.
Discrepancies are repaired only in the TXT without correcting the authoritative source or generator.

steps.name: Publish governed TXT release
actions: Apply the governed release naming convention without treating source examples as canonical unless separately governed.
Store the TXT in the governed distribution location.
Record file identity, registry version, release date, environment, releasing role, and change summary.
validation: The released TXT is traceable to the exact registry state from which it was generated.
failure_modes: Release identity is not traceable to a registry version.
A working file is distributed as though it were governed.

steps.name: Update project references and inspect deltas
actions: Point new and existing project workflows to the governed TXT or an explicitly controlled mirror derived from it.
Avoid unmanaged local master TXT files.
For existing projects, inspect unknown parameters, name/GUID collisions, deprecated Citizens, and missing required Citizens before remediation.
validation: Projects reference the governed release path or an approved controlled mirror.
Existing-project deviations are identified rather than silently overwritten.
failure_modes: An unmanaged local TXT becomes de facto authority.
Existing project identities are silently replaced without delta review.

steps.name: Archive superseded releases
actions: Move superseded TXT releases to the governed archive or mark them as superseded/deprecated.
Retain prior releases for traceability, forensic comparison, and governed rollback where applicable.
validation: Historical releases remain traceable and are clearly distinguished from the current release.
failure_modes: Superseded releases remain indistinguishable from the current governed release.

outputs: Governed shared-parameter TXT release derived from the registry
Release metadata linking the TXT to a registry state
governance_notes: The TXT is a derived distribution artifact and never supersedes the registry as shared-parameter authority.
Source example filenames and folder paths are noncanonical until separately governed.
Existing project differences are inspected and reconciled; they are not silently overwritten by release generation.

provenance.source_title: Instruction Set for Generating SP TXT from Shared Parameter Registry
provenance.migration_note: Source is draft L6 guidance. Organization-specific labels, paths, and example filenames were neutralized; registry authority, release validation, and archive logic were preserved.
